assignedReviews.card_evidence: Karl Ereky
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to explain: a. how typhoons develop, and b. why the Philippines is prone to typhoons
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the origin of the term biotechnology, not about typhoon development or why the Philippines is prone to typhoons. No instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Karl Ereky
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how solar energy contributes to the occurrence of land and sea breezes, monsoons, and the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses biotechnology terminology, not solar energy contributions to breezes, monsoons, or ITCZ. Completely unrelated to the competency.

copy.en:
Who first used the word biotechnology?

Karl Ereky, a Hungarian engineer, coined the term in 1919 to describe making products from raw materials with the help of living organisms!
copy.tl:
Sino ang unang gumamit ng salitang biotechnology?

Si Karl Ereky, isang inhinyerong Hungarian, ang nag-imbento ng termino noong 1919 para ilarawan ang paggawa ng mga produkto mula sa hilaw na materyales sa tulong ng mga buhay na organismo!
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang unang migamit sa pulong nga biotechnology?

Si Karl Ereky, usa ka Hungarian nga engineer, ang nag-imbento sa termino sa 1919 aron ihulagway ang paghimo ug mga produkto gamit ang tabang sa mga buhing organismo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Keep the digital balance clean and dry
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the formation of ions as either the loss or gain of electrons to produce ionic bonds, using examples, such as the formation of sodium chloride
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives care/maintenance instructions for a digital balance. It does not address ion formation, electron loss/gain, or ionic bonds, which are the core of G9-M-5.

copy.en: Keep the digital balance clean and dry, and avoid pressing too hard on the buttons to prevent damage.
copy.tl: Panatilihing malinis at tuyo ang digital balance, at iwasan ang masyadong malakas na pagpindot sa mga button para hindi masira.
copy.bis: Hupti nga limpyo ug uga ang digital balance, ug likayi ang kusog kaayo nga pagpugos sa mga button aron dili maguba.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Keeping all other factors the same as control variables
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes, such as wind and water, or by people, such as pushing, pulling, rolling, and carrying
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains control variables in a fair test, which is experimental design content. G3-F-1 is about exploring and demonstrating ways to make objects move (wind, water, pushing, pulling, etc.). The card provides no instructional support for moving objects and is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: Keeping all other factors the same as control variables ensures that only the independent variable can affect the dependent variable in a fair test.
copy.tl: Ang pagpapanatili ng lahat ng ibang factor bilang control variables ay tumitiyak na ang independent variable lang ang makakaapekto sa dependent variable sa fair test.
copy.bis: Ang pagpabilin sa tanang uban nga factor isip control variables magsiguro nga ang independent variable lang ang makaapekto sa dependent variable sa fair test.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: thermal expansion makes the water take up more space as it heats
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the role of the solute and solvent in a solution
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about thermal expansion of water when heated, not about the role of solute and solvent in a solution. No instructional support for G7-M-8.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: thermal expansion makes the water take up more space as it heats
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the formation of ions as either the loss or gain of electrons to produce ionic bonds, using examples, such as the formation of sodium chloride
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses thermal expansion of water, not ion formation, electron loss/gain, or ionic bonding. Unrelated to G9-M-5.

copy.en: Do not fill a kettle to the brim when boiling water because thermal expansion makes the water take up more space as it heats.
copy.tl: Huwag punuin ang takure hanggang labi kapag magpapakulo ng tubig dahil ang thermal expansion ay nagpapalaki sa space na kinukuha ng tubig habang umiinit.
copy.bis: Ayaw pun-a ang takure hangtod sa ngilit kon magbukal ug tubig tungod kay ang thermal expansion magpadako sa space nga gikinahanglan sa tubig samtang moinit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The travelling car has kinetic energy because it is moving
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how different factors affect the solubility of a solute in a given solvent, such as heat
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches the concept of kinetic energy (moving vs. parked car), which is unrelated to the competency about factors affecting solubility of a solute in a solvent. The assigned code is for Grade 7 Matter (solubility), while the card content is Grade 8 Physics (kinetic energy).

copy.en:
Which has kinetic energy: a parked car or a travelling car?

The travelling car has kinetic energy because it is moving, while the parked car has none!
copy.tl:
Alin ang may kinetic energy: nakaparadang kotse o bumibiyaheng kotse?

Ang bumibiyaheng kotse ay may kinetic energy dahil ito ay gumagalaw, habang ang nakapark na kotse ay wala!
copy.bis:
Hain ang adunay kinetic energy: nagpark nga kotse o nagbiyahe nga kotse?

Ang nagbiyahe nga kotse adunay kinetic energy tungod kay kini naglihok, samtang ang nagpark nga kotse wala!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: knowing the distance helps you prepare for the trip
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the changes of state in terms of particle arrangement and energy changes: a. solid → liquid → vapor, and b. vapor → liquid → solid
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses travel distance and trip preparation, with no content about changes of state, particle arrangement, or energy changes.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts

assignedReviews.card_evidence: knowing the distance helps you prepare for the trip
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes
assignedReviews.reason: The card contains no information about heat energy or change of state processes; it is unrelated to this competency.

copy.en:
Do you need to know the distance you will travel before you go?

Yes, knowing the distance helps you prepare for the trip and estimate how much time and fuel you will need.
copy.tl:
Kailangan mo bang malaman ang distansya na iyong lalakbayin bago ka umalis?

Oo, ang pag-alam sa distansya ay nakakatulong sa iyo na maghanda para sa biyahe at matantiya kung gaano karaming oras at gasolina ang kakailanganin mo.
copy.bis:
Kinahanglan ba nimo mahibaloan ang distansya nga imong biyaheon sa dili ka pa molarga?

Oo, ang pagkahibalo sa distansya makatabang kanimo sa pagpangandam alang sa biyahe ug pagbanabana kung pila ka oras ug gasolina ang imong gikinahanglan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wear safety goggles and a lab coat or apron during experiments
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how relative and absolute dating techniques are used to determine the subdivisions of geologic time
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes laboratory safety gear and hand-washing procedures. The competency G9-E-5 requires describing relative and absolute dating techniques for geologic time subdivisions. There is no connection to geology, dating methods, or geologic time.

copy.en: Wear safety goggles and a lab coat or apron during experiments, and always wash your hands with soap and water after you finish.
copy.tl: Magsuot ng safety goggles at lab coat o apron habang nag-eeksperimento, at laging maghugas ng kamay gamit ang sabon at tubig pagkatapos.
copy.bis: Pagsul-ob ug safety goggles ug lab coat o apron samtang nag-eksperimento, ug kanunay paghugas sa kamot gamit ang sabon ug tubig pagkahuman.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A laboratory thermometer measures temperatures of substances
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how relative and absolute dating techniques are used to determine the subdivisions of geologic time
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a laboratory thermometer and its use for measuring substance temperatures, which is unrelated to relative and absolute dating techniques or subdivisions of geologic time. The competency concerns geologic time dating methods, not temperature measurement.

copy.en: A laboratory thermometer measures temperatures of substances like freezing point and boiling point, not human body temperature.
copy.tl: Ang laboratory thermometer ay sumusukat ng temperatura ng mga substance tulad ng freezing point at boiling point, hindi ang temperatura ng katawan ng tao.
copy.bis: Ang laboratory thermometer nagsukod sa temperatura sa mga substance sama sa freezing point ug boiling point, dili sa temperatura sa lawas sa tawo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Some animals like frogs and swans can live both on land and in water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to explore and record how and when the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars can be seen moving across the sky
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses animals that live on land and water; it has no content about the Sun, Moon, planets, stars, or their apparent motion across the sky.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Some animals like frogs and swans can live both on land and in water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate the rotation of the Earth on its axis using a globe to explain day and night
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about animal habitats, not Earth's rotation, day/night, or globe demonstrations.

copy.en: Some animals like frogs and swans can live both on land and in water, so they can walk, hop, or swim whenever they need to.
copy.tl: Ang ilang mga hayop tulad ng palaka at swan ay kayang mabuhay sa lupa at sa tubig, kaya maaari silang maglakad, lumukso, o lumangoy kung kinakailangan.
copy.bis: Ang pipila ka mananap sama sa baki ug swan makapuyo sa yuta ug sa tubig, busa makalakaw, makalukso, o makalangoy sila kon gikinahanglan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The large intestine is where the formation and propelling of feces toward the rectum for elimination occur.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the function of the large intestine in the digestive system, which has no relation to the competency about investigating reflection and refraction of light using mirrors, lenses, and prisms.

copy.en: The large intestine is where the formation and propelling of feces toward the rectum for elimination occur.
copy.tl: Ang large intestine ang lugar kung saan nabubuo at itinutulak ang dumi patungo sa rectum para mailabas.
copy.bis: Ang large intestine mao ang lugar diin maporma ug itulod ang hugaw padulong sa rectum aron mawagtang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: During the last quarter phase, the half lighted part of the moon can be seen again on the third week of the month.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how relative and absolute dating techniques are used to determine the subdivisions of geologic time
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a lunar phase (last quarter), which is an astronomy topic. G9-E-5 concerns relative and absolute dating techniques for geologic time subdivisions, which is unrelated to moon phases.

copy.en: During the last quarter phase, the half lighted part of the moon can be seen again on the third week of the month.
copy.tl: Sa last quarter phase, ang kalahating maliwanag na bahagi ng buwan ay makikitang muli sa ikatlong linggo ng buwan.
copy.bis: Sa last quarter phase, ang katunga nga hayag nga parte sa bulan makita pag-usab sa ikatulo nga semana sa bulan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: every new layer of cooled lava adds more height and mass
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the formation of covalent bonds using a molecule of water and a molecule of carbon dioxide
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes volcanic eruptions building mountains through cooled lava layers. G9-M-7 requires explaining covalent bond formation using water and carbon dioxide molecules, which is a chemistry topic unrelated to volcanic activity.

copy.en: The same eruptions that grow islands also build mountains, because every new layer of cooled lava adds more height and mass to the volcano's slopes.
copy.tl: Ang mga pagputok na nagpapalaki ng mga isla ay siya ring bumubuo ng mga bundok, dahil ang bawat bagong patong ng lumamig na lava ay nagdaragdag ng taas at laki sa mga gilid ng bulkan.
copy.bis: Ang mga pagbuto nga nagpadako sa mga isla mao usab ang naghimo sa mga bukid, tungod kay ang matag bag-ong patong sa nibugnaw nga lava nagdugang og taas ug kadako sa mga kilid sa bulkan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The law of reflection says the incident ray, the reflected ray, and the normal line all lie in the same plane.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate various techniques in separating mixtures, such as decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, and using magnets
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches the law of reflection (optics/physics), which has no connection to separating mixtures (decantation, winnowing, filtering, etc.). The assigned competency is about matter and mixture separation techniques, so the tag is unrelated.

copy.en: The law of reflection says the incident ray, the reflected ray, and the normal line all lie in the same plane.
copy.tl: Sinasabi ng law of reflection na ang incident ray, ang reflected ray, at ang normal line ay nasa iisang plane o patag na lapad.
copy.bis: Ang law of reflection nag-ingon nga ang incident ray, ang reflected ray, ug ang normal line anaa sa samang plane o patag nga lapad.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Leaching is the downward movement of tiny particles and dissolved minerals through the soil as water trickles down.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how plate tectonics can be used to explain the formation of the largest mountain ranges on Earth including the Himalayas and the Andes mountains
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes soil leaching, which is unrelated to plate tectonics or the formation of mountain ranges such as the Himalayas and Andes.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the structures, movements and events that occur at each type of plate boundary
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes soil leaching, which has no connection to plate boundaries, their structures, movements, or associated events.

copy.en: Leaching is the downward movement of tiny particles and dissolved minerals through the soil as water trickles down.
copy.tl: Ang leaching ay ang paggalaw pababa ng maliliit na particle at natunaw na mineral sa lupa habang tumutulo ang tubig pababa.
copy.bis: Ang leaching mao ang paglihok paubos sa gagmayng particle ug natunaw nga mineral sa yuta samtang motulo ang tubig paubos.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A cutting should include at least one leaf node
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe electromagnetic radiation (EMR) as energy that is created by the vibrations of electrically charged particles which allows it to travel through materials or space as transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about plant cutting and leaf nodes, with no content on electromagnetic radiation, charged particles, or transverse waves.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A cutting should include at least one leaf node
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, at home and in the local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about plant propagation, not sources or uses of light, sound, or heat energy.

copy.en: A cutting should include at least one leaf node, the small bump on a stem where leaves grow, because that is where new roots will emerge.
copy.tl: Ang cutting ay dapat may kasamang kahit isang leaf node, ang maliit na bukol sa sanga kung saan tumutubo ang mga dahon, dahil doon lalabas ang mga bagong ugat.
copy.bis: Ang cutting kinahanglan adunay labing menos usa ka leaf node, ang gamay nga bukol sa sanga diin motubo ang mga dahon, kay didto mogawas ang mga bag-ong gamot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Emigration, when individuals leave a population to live elsewhere
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses emigration as a density-dependent population factor, which is unrelated to tropical cyclone weather conditions. No weather content is present.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Emigration, when individuals leave a population to live elsewhere
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: examine a local weather chart to make simple interpretations about the local weather and describe and practice safety precautions to use during poor or extreme weather conditions
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about population ecology, not weather charts, local weather interpretation, or safety precautions. It does not support any part of this competency.

copy.en: Emigration, when individuals leave a population to live elsewhere, is a density-dependent factor that can reduce the size of the original group.
copy.tl: Ang emigration, kapag umaalis ang mga indibidwal sa isang population para manirahan sa ibang lugar, ay isang density-dependent factor na nakakapagpababa sa bilang ng orihinal na grupo.
copy.bis: Ang emigration, kon mobiya ang mga indibidwal sa usa ka population aron mopuyo sa laing lugar, usa ka density-dependent factor nga makapamenos sa gidaghanon sa orihinal nga grupo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Land animals like horses and carabaos use their strong legs to walk, run, and carry their bodies across the ground.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes animal locomotion using legs, which is a life science topic. G5-E-11 requires describing the general structure of the solar system, celestial objects, and their features/composition. There is no connection to the solar system or any earth/space content.

copy.en: Land animals like horses and carabaos use their strong legs to walk, run, and carry their bodies across the ground.
copy.tl: Ang mga hayop sa lupa tulad ng kabayo at kalabaw ay gumagamit ng malalakas na binti para maglakad, tumakbo, at dalhin ang kanilang katawan sa lupa.
copy.bis: Ang mga mananap sa yuta sama sa kabayo ug kabaw mogamit sa ilang kusgan nga mga tiil aron molakaw, modagan, ug modala sa ilang lawas sa yuta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most menstrual periods last from 3 to 5 days
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe a valence electron as an electron in the outer shell of an atom that can take part in formation of bonds
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the duration of menstrual periods, a biology/health topic. The competency G9-M-3 requires describing a valence electron in the outer shell of an atom for bond formation, a chemistry concept. There is no instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: Most menstrual periods last from 3 to 5 days, though the exact number of days can vary from one female to another.
copy.tl: Karamihan ng menstrual period ay tumatagal ng 3 hanggang 5 araw, pero maaaring mag-iba ang bilang ng araw sa bawat babae.
copy.bis: Kadaghanan sa menstrual period molungtad og 3 hangtod 5 ka adlaw, apan mahimong magkalahi ang gidaghanon sa adlaw sa matag babaye.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The type of lens and the distance of the object from the lens
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate sexual from asexual reproduction in terms of: a) number of parents involved, and b) similarities of offspring to parents
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses lens types and image formation, which is an optics/physics topic. G7-L-7 is about differentiating sexual from asexual reproduction, a biology competency with no connection to lenses or image formation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The type of lens and the distance of the object from the lens
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses lens types and image formation, which is an optics/physics topic. G3-L-3 is about characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce), a biology competency with no connection to lenses or image formation.

copy.en: The type of lens and the distance of the object from the lens are the two main things that decide what kind of image will form.
copy.tl: Ang uri ng lens at ang layo ng object mula sa lens ang dalawang pangunahing bagay na nagdedesisyon kung anong uri ng image ang mabubuo.
copy.bis: Ang klase sa lens ug ang gilay-on sa object gikan sa lens mao ang duha ka pangunang butang nga magdesisyon kon unsang klase sa image ang maporma.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A lesser force makes an object travel a shorter distance
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why ancient human cultures relied on constellations to indicate directions and verify seasons
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about force and motion (a gentle push moves a toy car a shorter distance). It has no content about constellations, directions, or seasons, which are the focus of G6-E-9.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A lesser force makes an object travel a shorter distance
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how natural objects in the sky affect activities of people
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses force and distance, not natural objects in the sky or their effects on people's activities. It does not support G3-E-8 in any way.

copy.en: A lesser force makes an object travel a shorter distance, so a gentle push moves a toy car only a little way.
copy.tl: Ang mahinang force ay nagpapaikli ng distansya ng isang bagay, kaya ang marahang tulak ay kaunti lang ang magagalaw sa laruang sasakyan.
copy.bis: Ang hinay nga force nagpamubo sa distansya sa usa ka butang, busa ang hinay nga pagtulak mopalihok lang ug gamay sa dulaan nga sakyanan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Lewis Electron Dot Structure of sodium shows the symbol Na with one dot, because sodium has one valence electron.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and describe some of the materials formed during volcanic eruptions in the Philippines
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches the Lewis electron dot structure of sodium, a chemistry concept about valence electrons. G6-E-4 requires identifying and describing materials formed during volcanic eruptions in the Philippines. There is no connection to volcanic materials or earth science.

copy.en: The Lewis Electron Dot Structure of sodium shows the symbol Na with one dot, because sodium has one valence electron.
copy.tl: Ang Lewis Electron Dot Structure ng sodium ay nagpapakita ng simbolong Na na may isang tuldok, dahil may isang valence electron ang sodium.
copy.bis: Ang Lewis Electron Dot Structure sa sodium nagpakita sa simbolo nga Na nga adunay usa ka tuldok, tungod kay adunay usa ka valence electron ang sodium.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A life cycle repeats itself for each new generation of life
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain what volcanoes are and how they are formed
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about biological life cycles, not volcanoes or their formation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A life cycle repeats itself for each new generation of life
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the structures, movements and events that occur at each type of plate boundary
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses organism life cycles, not plate boundary structures, movements, or events.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A life cycle repeats itself for each new generation of life
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how the subduction of an oceanic plate impacts on the plate above it
assignedReviews.reason: The card has no content about oceanic plate subduction or its impact on an overlying plate.

copy.en: A human's life cycle repeats when an adult has a baby, and that baby will grow through the same stages!
copy.tl: Ang life cycle ng tao ay umuulit kapag ang adult ay nagkaroon ng baby na tutubo sa parehong mga yugto!
copy.bis: Ang life cycle sa tao magbalik-balik kung ang adult adunay baby, ug kana nga baby motubo sa parehas nga mga yugto!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Comparing life with and without inventions
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the structures, movements and events that occur at each type of plate boundary
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the impact of inventions on daily life, comparing past and present tasks. It contains no information about plate boundaries, their structures, movements, or events, which is the subject of G10-E-2.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Comparing life with and without inventions
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how the subduction of an oceanic plate impacts on the plate above it
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about inventions and their effects on human activities, not about oceanic plate subduction or its impact on the overriding plate. There is no geological content.

copy.en: Comparing life with and without inventions shows their impact: before, people walked far, wrote letters, and made fire, but now tasks are faster and easier.
copy.tl: Ang paghahambing ng buhay noon at ngayon ay nagpapakita ng epekto ng mga imbensyon: dati, naglalakad nang malayo ang mga tao, nagsusulat ng liham, at gumagawa ng apoy, pero ngayon mas mabilis at mas madali na ang mga gawain.
copy.bis: Ang pagtandi sa kinabuhi kaniadto ug karon nagpakita sa epekto sa mga imbensyon: sa una, ang mga tao naglakaw ug layo, nagsulat ug sulat, ug naghimo ug kalayo, apan karon mas paspas ug mas sayon na ang mga buluhaton.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate ways to minimize harmful changes in materials, such as restriction of burning of waste materials, and care in handling reactive materials

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: G4-M-3 concerns chemical properties of materials (burning, reactivity, degradability). The card is about light reflection, unrelated to chemical properties of materials.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When light hits a surface and bounces back toward its source, that property is called reflection.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that changes in materials can be harmful to living and non-living things in the environment, such as trash disposal, and burning household materials
assignedReviews.reason: G3-M-6 explains harmful changes in materials to living/non-living things. The card describes light reflection, which is not a material change or environmental harm.

copy.en: When light hits a surface and bounces back toward its source, that property is called reflection.
copy.tl: Kapag tumama ang liwanag sa isang surface at tumalbog pabalik sa pinanggalingan nito, ang property na iyon ay tinatawag na reflection.
copy.bis: Kon moigo ang kahayag sa usa ka surface ug mobalik pabalik sa gigikanan, kana nga property gitawag ug reflection.

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses light as a communication medium, not current, voltage, resistance, or series/parallel circuits. It does not support the G9-F-7 competency in any way.

copy.en: Light energy is used for communication, such as traffic lights that tell drivers when to stop and go.
copy.tl: Ang light energy ay ginagamit para sa komunikasyon, tulad ng mga traffic light na nagsasabi sa mga driver kung kailan hihinto at kailan aalis.
copy.bis: Ang light energy gigamit alang sa komunikasyon, sama sa mga traffic light nga nagsulti sa mga driver kung kanus-a mohunong ug kanus-a molakaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Light spreads out in all directions from its source
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a simple electromagnet and observe and record its properties
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes light spreading from a source, which is unrelated to making an electromagnet or observing its properties.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: assemble and draw a simple circuit using batteries, wires, switch, and bulb and/or toy motor or buzzer

copy.bis: Ang mga liquid adunay lain-laing kolor, sama sa itom, pula, ug dalag, apan ang uban nga liquid walay kolor.

copy.en: Liquid particles have spaces between them and less attractive force, so they flow easily and can be compressed a little.
copy.tl: Ang mga particles ng liquid ay may pagitan at mahinang attractive force, kaya madali silang dumaloy at maaaring i-compress nang kaunti.
copy.bis: Ang mga particles sa liquid adunay mga luna ug huyang nga attractive force, mao nga dali silang modagayday ug mahimong i-compress og gamay.

copy.tl: Sa panahon ng pagputok ng bulkan, dapat kang makinig sa mga ulat ng balita at bigyang-pansin ang mga babala mula sa mga lokal na awtoridad upang manatiling ligtas.
copy.bis: Sa panahon sa pagbuto sa bulkan, kinahanglan maminaw ka sa mga balita ug hatagan og pagtagad ang mga pasidaan sa mga lokal nga awtoridad aron magpabiling luwas.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches triangulation of an earthquake epicenter using seismograph stations. G5-L-2 is about identifying parts of the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) and how they work. There is no respiratory system content or any living-things content on the card.

copy.en:
How many seismograph stations are needed to locate an epicenter?

Three! Each station gives a distance, and where the three circles meet is the epicenter.
copy.tl:
Ilang seismograph stations ang kailangan para mahanap ang epicenter?

Tatlo! Bawat station ay nagbibigay ng distansya, at kung saan nagtagpo ang tatlong bilog ay ang epicenter.
copy.bis:
Pila ka seismograph stations ang gikinahanglan para makit-an ang epicenter?

Tulo! Ang matag station naghatag og distansya, ug diin magtagbo ang tulo ka lingin mao ang epicenter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Logging can reduce prey availability

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Logging can reduce prey availability
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: develop a timeline for the historical background of the development of the current Atomic Model that identifies tiny particles as atoms
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about habitat destruction and predator-prey relationships, not the historical development of the atomic model. G8-M-1 is unrelated to the card's subject matter.

copy.en: Logging can reduce prey availability and affect predator populations, because cutting down trees destroys the homes of the animals that predators eat.
copy.tl: Ang logging ay maaaring magbawas ng prey at makaapekto sa mga predator, dahil ang pagputol ng mga puno ay sumisira sa tirahan ng mga hayop na kinakain ng mga predator.
copy.bis: Ang logging makapakunhod sa prey ug makaapekto sa mga predator, tungod kay ang pagputol sa mga kahoy makaguba sa pinuy-anan sa mga mananap nga gikaon sa mga predator.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the formation of covalent bonds using a molecule of water and a molecule of carbon dioxide
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses Earth's tilt and day length, which is an astronomy/earth science concept. It provides no information about covalent bond formation using water or carbon dioxide molecules.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The hemisphere that is tilted toward the Sun has longer daytime
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe a valence electron as an electron in the outer shell of an atom that can take part in formation of bonds
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the effect of Earth's tilt on daytime length, not about valence electrons or chemical bonding. It does not support the competency in any way.

copy.en: The hemisphere that is tilted toward the Sun has longer daytime because it stays in the Sun's light for more hours each day.
copy.tl: Ang hemisphere na nakatagilid patungo sa Araw ay may mas mahabang araw dahil mas maraming oras itong nananatili sa liwanag ng Araw kada araw.
copy.bis: Ang hemisphere nga nakiling paingon sa Adlaw adunay mas taas nga adlaw tungod kay mas daghan kini og oras nga magpabilin sa kahayag sa Adlaw kada adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Love waves travel faster than Rayleigh waves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different types of volcanoes found around the world according to their: a. activity b. type of eruption c. location in the crust
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the relative speed of seismic surface waves (Love vs Rayleigh) after an earthquake. G8-E-3 is about describing different types of volcanoes according to activity, eruption type, and crustal location. Seismic wave speed is unrelated to volcano classification.

copy.en: Love waves travel faster than Rayleigh waves, so after an earthquake, the sharp sideways shaking often arrives before the rolling motion.
copy.tl: Mas mabilis ang Love waves kaysa Rayleigh waves, kaya pagkatapos ng lindol, ang matalim na side-to-side na pagyanig ay madalas na nauuna bago ang pagulong.
copy.bis: Mas paspas ang Love waves kaysa Rayleigh waves, mao nga human sa linog, ang hait nga kilid-kilid nga pag-uyog kasagarang moabot una sa pagligid.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An ecosystem with low biodiversity
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that electricity is a flow of electrons and show appreciation for the need to observe safe measures in handling electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses ecosystem biodiversity and fragility, which is unrelated to electricity as a flow of electrons or safe handling of electricity.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An ecosystem with low biodiversity
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe and explain the need for safety precautions in handling household electrical devices
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses ecosystem biodiversity and fragility, which is unrelated to safety precautions for household electrical devices.

copy.en: An ecosystem with low biodiversity contains fewer species, making it more fragile because the loss of even one species can have a big impact.
copy.tl: Ang isang ecosystem na may mababang biodiversity ay naglalaman ng mas kaunting species, kaya mas marupok ito dahil ang pagkawala ng kahit isang species ay maaaring magdulot ng malaking epekto.
copy.bis: Ang usa ka ecosystem nga adunay ubos nga biodiversity adunay mas diyutay nga species, mao nga mas huyang kini tungod kay ang pagkawala sa bisan usa ka species mahimong adunay dako nga epekto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Choosing energy-saving appliances with low power ratings reduces electrical consumption
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how solar energy contributes to the occurrence of land and sea breezes, monsoons, and the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about electrical consumption and appliance power ratings, with no mention of solar energy, breezes, monsoons, or ITCZ. It does not support the competency.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses energy-saving appliances and electricity use, not landforms, bodies of water, or their influence on the environment. It is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: Choosing energy-saving appliances with low power ratings reduces electrical consumption because they use fewer watts to do the same job.
copy.tl: Ang pagpili ng energy-saving appliances na may mababang power ratings ay nakakabawas ng konsumo ng kuryente dahil mas kaunting watts ang ginagamit nila para sa parehong trabaho.
copy.bis: Ang pagpili sa energy-saving appliances nga adunay ubos nga power ratings makapakgang sa konsumo sa kuryente tungod kay mas gamay nga watts ang ilang gamiton para sa parehas nga trabaho.

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a coverslip placement technique to avoid air bubbles. It does not address particle motion, spacing, attraction, or temperature effects on particles, which are the core of G7-M-3.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to certain changes in temperature, such as changes when wood or coal are burned
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about a microscope slide preparation technique, not about changes in material properties due to temperature (e.g., burning wood or coal). No temperature-related change is described.

copy.en: Lower the coverslip onto the slide at an angle! This pushes out air bubbles that blur your view.
copy.tl: Ibaba ang coverslip sa slide nang nakatagilid para itulak palabas ang mga bula ng hangin na nagpapalabo sa tingin!
copy.bis: Ipaubos ang coverslip sa slide nga nagtakilid aron itulod pagawas ang mga bula sa hangin nga nagpalubog sa pagtan-aw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The troposphere is the lowest layer of the atmosphere, and it holds about 75% of all atmospheric gases because gravity pulls them close to Earth.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why physical changes are reversible, and chemical changes are irreversible
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the troposphere and atmospheric gas distribution due to gravity. It contains no information about physical changes being reversible or chemical changes being irreversible, which is the subject of G6-M-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The troposphere is the lowest layer of the atmosphere, and it holds about 75% of all atmospheric gases because gravity pulls them close to Earth.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that the formation of new bonds or the breaking of existing bonds constitutes a chemical change and the formation of a new substance
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not discuss bond formation, bond breaking, chemical change, or new substance formation. It is entirely about atmospheric layers and gravity, unrelated to G9-M-2.

copy.en: The troposphere is the lowest layer of the atmosphere, and it holds about 75% of all atmospheric gases because gravity pulls them close to Earth.
copy.tl: Ang troposphere ang pinakamababang layer ng atmosphere, at hawak nito ang halos 75% ng lahat ng gas sa atmosphere dahil hinihila ng gravity ang mga ito palapit sa Earth.
copy.bis: Ang troposphere mao ang pinakaubos nga layer sa atmosphere, ug gikuptan niini ang mga 75% sa tanang gas sa atmosphere tungod kay gibira sa gravity ang mga kini paduol sa Earth.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Lung cancer is the uncontrolled growth of abnormal cells or tumors in the lungs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate proper handling and disposal of materials according to their properties, such as reusing objects, disposing of excess oil into garbage, and recycling paper, plastic or glass
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes lung cancer and its cause (smoking). It has no content about proper handling and disposal of materials, reusing, recycling, or any material properties. The competency is about waste/material management, which is unrelated to this health topic.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Lung cancer is the uncontrolled growth of abnormal cells or tumors in the lungs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify issues and concerns in the local community and how they could be addressed by science, such as the treatment of waste
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about lung cancer, not about local community issues and concerns addressed by science such as waste treatment. There is no connection to identifying community issues or science-based solutions. The topic is entirely unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: Lung cancer is the uncontrolled growth of abnormal cells or tumors in the lungs, often caused by cigarette smoking.
copy.tl: Ang lung cancer ay ang hindi mapigil na pagdami ng abnormal na mga cell o tumor sa baga, na kadalasang sanhi ng paninigarilyo.
copy.bis: Ang lung cancer mao ang dili mapugngan nga pagdaghan sa abnormal nga mga cell o tumor sa baga, nga kasagarang hinungdan sa pagpanigarilyo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The lungs are the main organs of the respiratory system
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the anatomy of the lungs (lobes of the respiratory system), which has no relation to the competency about speed as distance over time. The assigned code is for force/motion/energy, not biology.

copy.en: The lungs are the main organs of the respiratory system, with the right lung having three lobes and the left lung having two lobes.
copy.tl: Ang baga ang pangunahing organ ng respiratory system, kung saan ang kanang baga ay may tatlong lobes at ang kaliwang baga ay may dalawang lobes.
copy.bis: Ang baga mao ang pangunang organ sa respiratory system, diin ang tuo nga baga adunay tulo ka lobes ug ang wala nga baga adunay duha ka lobes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why is a swollen lymph node sore?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why a lymph node becomes sore during infection. It does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations, and it does not explain how body systems work together (e.g., digestion and excretion). The content is unrelated to the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why is a swollen lymph node sore?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The competency asks for simple descriptions of how the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory systems work. The card discusses lymph nodes (immune/lymphatic system) and a symptom, not any of the listed systems or their functioning.

copy.en:
Why is a swollen lymph node sore?

When it grows fast fighting an infection, its covering stretches and hurts. A node battling an ordinary illness is usually just tender and soft.
copy.tl:
Bakit minsan masakit ang namamagang kulani?

Kapag mabilis itong lumaki dahil sa impeksyon, naninikip ang balot nito kaya nananakit. Karaniwang malambot at bahagyang masakit lang ang kulani na nilalabanan ang ordinaryong sakit.
copy.bis:
Ngano usahay sakit ang naghubag nga kulani?

Kon paspas kini modako tungod sa impeksyon, moinat ang sapot niini mao nga masakit. Kasagaran humok ug gamay ra sakit ang kulani nga nakig-away sa ordinaryong sakit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because they are large molecules composed of thousands of covalently connected atoms!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: create a scale drawing to represent relative thicknesses of the layers of Earth's interior, including the crust, lithosphere, asthenosphere, mantle, outer core, and inner core

G9-E-8 requires creating a scale drawing of Earth's interior layers (crust, lithosphere, asthenosphere, mantle, outer core, inner core). There is no connection to Earth's structure or scale drawing.

copy.en:
Why are biomolecules called macromolecules?

Because they are large molecules composed of thousands of covalently connected atoms!
copy.tl:
Bakit tinatawag na macromolecules ang biomolecules?

Dahil ang mga ito ay malalaking molecule na binubuo ng libo-libong covalently connected atoms!
copy.bis:
Ngano gitawag ug macromolecules ang biomolecules?

Tungod kay kini mga dagkong molecule nga gilangkuban sa libo-libo ka covalently connected atoms!

The card provides no direct or prerequisite support for this competency.

copy.en: Magma temperature reflects the melting points of its mineral components, with some basalts reaching over 1200°C while rhyolites are often below 900°C.
copy.tl: Ang temperatura ng magma ay sumasalamin sa melting points ng mga mineral component nito, kung saan ang ilang basalts ay umaabot sa higit 1200°C habang ang rhyolites ay madalas na mas mababa sa 900°C.
copy.bis: Ang temperatura sa magma nagpakita sa melting points sa mga mineral component niini, diin ang uban nga basalts moabot sa kapin sa 1200°C samtang ang rhyolites sagad ubos sa 900°C.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Magnesium oxide, MgO, forms when magnesium loses two electrons
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: Interpret PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring (Alert Levels) to demonstrate what to do before, during, and after a volcanic eruption
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches ionic bond formation in magnesium oxide, a chemistry topic. G6-E-5 requires interpreting PHIVOLCS volcano alert levels and demonstrating actions before, during, and after a volcanic eruption. There is no connection to volcanoes, alert levels, or safety procedures.

copy.en: Magnesium oxide, MgO, forms when magnesium loses two electrons to become Mg2+ and oxygen gains two electrons to become O2-.
copy.tl: Ang magnesium oxide, MgO, ay nabubuo kapag ang magnesium ay naglalabas ng dalawang electrons para maging Mg2+ at ang oxygen ay kumukuha ng dalawang electrons para maging O2-.
copy.bis: Ang magnesium oxide, MgO, maporma kon ang magnesium magpagawas og duha ka electrons aron mahimong Mg2+ ug ang oxygen mokuha og duha ka electrons aron mahimong O2-.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Everyday objects like paper clips, nails, bolts, and keys can be magnetic
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: Interpret PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring (Alert Levels) to demonstrate what to do before, during, and after a volcanic eruption
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses magnetism of everyday objects, which is unrelated to interpreting PHIVOLCS volcano alert levels or volcanic eruption safety.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Everyday objects like paper clips, nails, bolts, and keys can be magnetic
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: refer to the local disaster readiness plans to demonstrate what to do during and after an earthquake
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses magnetism of everyday objects, which is unrelated to earthquake disaster readiness plans or earthquake safety procedures.

copy.en: Everyday objects like paper clips, nails, bolts, and keys can be magnetic because they are often made of iron or steel.
copy.tl: Ang mga pang-araw-araw na bagay tulad ng paper clips, pako, bolts, at susi ay maaaring magnetic dahil kadalasang gawa ang mga ito sa bakal o steel.
copy.bis: Ang mga adlaw-adlaw nga butang sama sa paper clips, lansang, bolts, ug yawi mahimong magnetic tungod kay kasagarang hinimo kini sa puthaw o steel.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The magnetic quantum number, written as ml, describes how an orbital behaves in a magnetic field
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw the structure of an atom in terms of the nucleus and electron shells
assignedReviews.reason: G8-M-2 requires drawing the structure of an atom in terms of the nucleus and electron shells. The magnetic quantum number is a quantum mechanical concept about orbital orientation, not about drawing atomic structure or electron shells at the Grade 8 level. It does not support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The magnetic quantum number, written as ml, describes how an orbital behaves in a magnetic field
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate the subatomic particles protons, neutrons, and electrons in terms of their symbol, mass, charge, and location within an atom
assignedReviews.reason: G8-M-3 requires differentiating subatomic particles (protons, neutrons, electrons) by symbol, mass, charge, and location. The magnetic quantum number is not a subatomic particle and does not address any of these differentiating criteria. It is unrelated to this competency.

copy.en: The magnetic quantum number, written as ml, describes how an orbital behaves in a magnetic field, with values like +1, 0, and -1 for p orbitals.
copy.tl: Ang magnetic quantum number, na isinusulat bilang ml, ay naglalarawan kung paano kumikilos ang isang orbital sa magnetic field, na may mga value tulad ng +1, 0, at -1 para sa p orbitals.
copy.bis: Ang magnetic quantum number, nga gisulat isip ml, naghulagway kon unsaon paglihok sa usa ka orbital sa magnetic field, nga adunay mga value sama sa +1, 0, ug -1 alang sa p orbitals.

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses magnification multiples, which is an optics concept unrelated to the particle model of matter, particle motion, spacing, attraction, or temperature effects described in G7-M-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Magnification is measured in multiples like 2x, 4x, and 10x
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses magnification multiples, which is unrelated to the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume described in G5-M-3.

copy.en: Magnification is measured in multiples like 2x, 4x, and 10x, meaning the object is enlarged to twice, four times, or ten times its real size.
copy.tl: Ang magnification ay sinusukat sa multiples tulad ng 2x, 4x, at 10x, ibig sabihin ang bagay ay pinalaki ng dalawang beses, apat na beses, o sampung beses sa tunay nitong laki.
copy.bis: Ang magnification gisukod sa multiples sama sa 2x, 4x, ug 10x, nagpasabot nga ang butang gipadako sa duha ka beses, upat ka beses, o napulo ka beses sa tinuod nga gidak-on.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: Interpret PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring (Alert Levels) to demonstrate what to do before, during, and after a volcanic eruption
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes latitude lines and climate/season boundaries. It provides no information about PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring Alert Levels or what to do before, during, and after a volcanic eruption.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The equator, Tropic of Cancer, Tropic of Capricorn, Arctic Circle, and Antarctic Circle are major latitude lines that mark the boundaries of climate zones and seasons.
