assignedReviews.reason: The card is about latitude lines and climate zones, not about locating active or inactive volcanoes or assessing eruption risk to a local community.

copy.en: The equator, Tropic of Cancer, Tropic of Capricorn, Arctic Circle, and Antarctic Circle are major latitude lines that mark the boundaries of climate zones and seasons.
copy.tl: Ang equator, Tropic of Cancer, Tropic of Capricorn, Arctic Circle, at Antarctic Circle ay mga pangunahing latitude lines na nagmamarka sa mga hangganan ng climate zones at mga season.
copy.bis: Ang equator, Tropic of Cancer, Tropic of Capricorn, Arctic Circle, ug Antarctic Circle mao ang mga pangunang latitude lines nga nagtimaan sa mga utlanan sa climate zones ug mga season.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A hypothesis is your group's best guess about what you will find
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify solutions, which can be found at home and in school and that react with litmus indicator, as acids, bases, and salts
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains what a hypothesis is in a survey context, with an example about predicting waste types. It contains no information about solutions, litmus indicators, acids, bases, or salts, which are the focus of G7-M-11.

copy.en:
What is a hypothesis in a survey?

A hypothesis is your group's best guess about what you will find, like predicting that plastic wrappers will be the most common waste in the school canteen.
copy.tl:
Ano ang hypothesis sa isang survey?

Ang hypothesis ay ang pinakamahusay na hula ng iyong grupo tungkol sa inyong matutuklasan, tulad ng paghula na ang mga plastic wrapper ang magiging pinakakaraniwang basura sa canteen ng paaralan.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang hypothesis sa usa ka survey?

Ang hypothesis mao ang pinakamaayo nga tag-an sa imong grupo mahitungod sa inyong madiskobrehan, sama sa pagtagna nga ang mga plastic wrapper mao ang labing komon nga basura sa canteen sa eskwelahan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Continuously vibrating one end of a rope up and down creates a traveling wave
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate sexual from asexual reproduction in terms of: a) number of parents involved, and b) similarities of offspring to parents
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes creating a traveling wave on a rope, a physics/waves topic. G7-L-7 is about differentiating sexual from asexual reproduction in living things. There is no connection to reproduction, parents, or offspring.

copy.en: Continuously vibrating one end of a rope up and down creates a traveling wave that moves along the rope away from your hand.
copy.tl: Ang patuloy na pag-vibrate ng isang dulo ng lubid pataas at pababa ay lumilikha ng traveling wave na gumagalaw sa lubid palayo sa iyong kamay.
copy.bis: Ang padayon nga pag-vibrate sa usa ka pikas sa pisi pataas ug paubos makahimo ug traveling wave nga molihok sa pisi palayo sa imong kamot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Hydroelectric generators use electromagnetic induction
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: construct and annotate distance-time graphs and velocity-time graphs to represent uniform and non-uniform acceleration
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains electromagnetic induction in hydroelectric generators. G8-F-3 requires constructing and annotating distance-time and velocity-time graphs for uniform and non-uniform acceleration. The card has no connection to motion graphs or acceleration; it is about electricity generation via magnetic fields.

copy.en: Hydroelectric generators use electromagnetic induction, where a changing magnetic field from a spinning rotor induces an electric current in the stator.
copy.tl: Ang mga hydroelectric generator ay gumagamit ng electromagnetic induction, kung saan ang nagbabagong magnetic field mula sa umiikot na rotor ay nag-iinduce ng electric current sa stator.
copy.bis: Ang mga hydroelectric generator naggamit og electromagnetic induction, diin ang nag-usab nga magnetic field gikan sa nagtuyok nga rotor mag-induce og electric current sa stator.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: How much solution from 15 g oxalic acid for a 25% solution?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about calculating solution volume from mass and percentage, a chemistry/math topic. G3-F-2 concerns factors affecting the movement of objects (size, shape, heaviness, material, surface texture). There is no instructional support for movement of objects.

copy.en:
How much solution from 15 g oxalic acid for a 25% solution?

You need a total volume of 60 ml, because 15 g is 25% of 60 ml!
copy.tl:
Gaano karaming solution kung 15 g oxalic acid para sa 25% solution?

Kailangan mo ng kabuuang volume na 60 ml, dahil ang 15 g ay 25% ng 60 ml!
copy.bis:
Pila ka solution kung 15 g oxalic acid para sa 25% solution?

Kinahanglan nimo ang kinatibuk-ang volume nga 60 ml, tungod kay ang 15 g kay 25% sa 60 ml!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Malleable materials can be hammered and formed into shapes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the physical property of malleability in metals (gold, silver). It has no connection to tropical cyclone weather conditions before, during, or after a storm.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Malleable materials can be hammered and formed into shapes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to explain: a. how typhoons develop, and b. why the Philippines is prone to typhoons
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about malleable materials and jewelry making, not about typhoon development or why the Philippines is prone to typhoons. The assigned earth/space competency is unrelated to the card content.

copy.en: Malleable materials can be hammered and formed into shapes, like gold and silver being made into jewelry.
copy.tl: Ang mga malleable na materyales ay maaaring martilyuhin at hubugin sa iba't ibang hugis, tulad ng ginto at pilak na ginagawang alahas.
copy.bis: Ang mga malleable nga materyales mahimong martilyohon ug pormahon ngadto sa lain-laing porma, sama sa bulawan ug pilak nga gihimong alahas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Malunggay contains vitamin A, which helps keep your eyesight clear and sharp.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about vitamin A in malunggay and its benefit to eyesight. It does not address the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter) as required by G3-L-6.

copy.en:
What vitamin is in malunggay?

Malunggay contains vitamin A, which helps keep your eyesight clear and sharp.
copy.tl:
Anong bitamina meron ang malunggay?

May bitamina A ang malunggay, na mabuti para sa malinaw na paningin ng mata.
copy.bis:
Unsang bitamina ang naa sa kamunggay?

Ang kamunggay adunay bitamina A, nga maayo para sa tin-aw nga panan-aw sa mata.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mammals like lions, carabaos, kangaroos, dolphins, and pigs are viviparous
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes mammal reproduction (viviparity), which is unrelated to the competency about guided investigations on reflection and refraction of light using mirrors, lenses, and prisms.

copy.en: Mammals like lions, carabaos, kangaroos, dolphins, and pigs are viviparous, meaning they give birth to live young instead of laying eggs.
copy.tl: Ang mga mammal tulad ng lion, kalabaw, kangaroo, dolphin, at baboy ay viviparous, ibig sabihin nanganganak sila ng buhay na anak sa halip na mangitlog.
copy.bis: Ang mga mammal sama sa lion, kalabaw, kangaroo, dolphin, ug baboy kay viviparous, nagpasabot nga manganak sila ug buhi nga mga anak imbes nga mangitlog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Asthma is managed with inhalers or nebulizers that deliver medicine directly to the airways to reduce swelling and open the breathing tubes.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe conservation of energy in everyday situations involving gravity, such as when objects fall
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses asthma management with inhalers/nebulizers, which has no connection to conservation of energy in everyday situations involving gravity. It does not support the competency in any way.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Asthma is managed with inhalers or nebulizers that deliver medicine directly to the airways to reduce swelling and open the breathing tubes.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that energy is something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about medical treatment for asthma, not about energy as something that can cause change (light, sound, heat). It is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: Asthma is managed with inhalers or nebulizers that deliver medicine directly to the airways to reduce swelling and open the breathing tubes.
copy.tl: Ang hika ay pinamamahalaan gamit ang mga inhaler o nebulizer na nagdadala ng gamot diretso sa mga daanan ng hangin para mabawasan ang pamamaga at mabuksan ang mga tubong dinadaluyan ng hangin.
copy.bis: Ang hika gidumala pinaagi sa mga inhaler o nebulizer nga magdala ug tambal diretso sa mga agianan sa hangin aron mamenosan ang paghubag ug maablihan ang mga tubo sa pagginhawa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Guimaras is famous for growing what many call the sweetest mango
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the sweetness and fame of Guimaras mangoes, not about observing the outer parts of plants (leaves, roots, stems) or their roles in water and nutrient uptake. It does not support the competency.

copy.en: Guimaras is famous for growing what many call the sweetest mango in the Philippines, celebrated every year at MangoFiesta.
copy.tl: Ang Guimaras sa Visayas ay sikat sa pagiging pinaka-matamis na mangga ng Pilipinas; bawat taon, ipinagdiriwang ang MangoFiesta bilang pagkilala sa mangga ng lalawigan.
copy.bis: Ang Guimaras sa Visayas bantog sa pagmugna sa gikonsiderar nga pinaka-tam-is nga mangga sa Pilipinas; ang probinsya nagdayeg sa tinuig nga MangoFiesta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mangrove swamps protect coastal communities from strong waves and provide food and business opportunities for people.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses mangrove swamps' protective and economic roles, with no content about particle motion, spacing, attraction, or temperature effects. It does not support the G7-M-3 competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mangrove swamps protect coastal communities from strong waves and provide food and business opportunities for people.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about mangrove ecology and coastal benefits, not the properties of solids, liquids, or gases in terms of shape and volume. It is unrelated to G5-M-3.

copy.en: Mangrove swamps protect coastal communities from strong waves and provide food and business opportunities for people.
copy.tl: Ang mangrove swamps ay nagpoprotekta sa mga komunidad sa baybayin mula sa malalakas na alon at nagbibigay ng pagkain at kabuhayan para sa mga tao.
copy.bis: Ang mangrove swamps nagprotektar sa mga komunidad sa baybayon gikan sa kusog nga mga balud ug naghatag ug pagkaon ug panginabuhian alang sa mga tawo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the longest daytime in 2011 was about 13 hours on June 22
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of the water cycle in the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card provides data about day length in Manila, which relates to Earth's tilt and seasons, not the water cycle. It does not support the competency 'explain the role of the water cycle in the environment' in any way.

copy.en: In Manila, the longest daytime in 2011 was about 13 hours on June 22, while the shortest was about 11 hours and 16 minutes on December 22.
copy.tl: Sa Maynila, ang pinakamahabang araw noong 2011 ay humigit-kumulang 13 oras noong June 22, habang ang pinakamaikli ay humigit-kumulang 11 oras at 16 minuto noong December 22.
copy.bis: Sa Manila, ang labing taas nga adlaw sa 2011 kay mga 13 ka oras sa June 22, samtang ang labing mubo kay mga 11 ka oras ug 16 ka minuto sa December 22.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Humans have just 3 kinds of color receptors
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses color vision and the number of color receptors in mantis shrimp eyes. It does not describe outer body parts of animals (head, legs, wings) or their role in movement and food gathering, which is the focus of G3-L-4.

copy.en:
Which animal sees the most colors?

Humans have just 3 kinds of color receptors in our eyes — but the mantis shrimp has about 12! Imagine seeing that many more colors.
copy.tl:
Aling hayop ang nakakakita ng pinakamaraming kulay?

Ang tao ay may 3 klase lang ng color receptor sa mata — pero ang mantis shrimp ay may humigit-kumulang 12! Isipin mo kung gaano karaming kulay ang kaya nitong makita.
copy.bis:
Unsang hayop ang makakita og pinakadaghang kolor?

Ang tawo adunay 3 lang ka klase sa color receptor sa mata — apan ang mantis shrimp adunay mga 12! Handurawa kung pila ka daghan nga kolor ang makita niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The electric eel isn't the only animal that makes electricity
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about animals that produce electricity; it does not classify Philippine animals/plants by habitat using a drawing or diagram, nor does it mention terrestrial, aquatic, or aerial habitats.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The electric eel isn't the only animal that makes electricity
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups (mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians, fungi, bacteria, flowering/non-flowering plants). It only mentions three electric fish species.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The electric eel isn't the only animal that makes electricity
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes animals that generate electricity, not examples of animals that have changed to better suit their environment such as mimicry or camouflage. No adaptation concept is taught.

copy.en: The electric eel isn't the only animal that makes electricity — the electric ray and electric catfish can do it too.
copy.tl: Hindi lang ang electric eel ang nakagagawa ng kuryente — may iba pang hayop tulad ng electric ray at electric catfish na may ganitong kakayahan.
copy.bis: Dili lang ang electric eel ang makahimo og kuryente — aduna pay uban nga mananap sama sa electric ray ug electric catfish nga makahimo niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Without air resistance
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe using labeled diagrams the biotic and abiotic features of tropical rainforests, swamps, estuaries, mangrove forests, and coral reefs
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses projectile motion and the effect of air resistance on mass in a vacuum, which is physics content. G9-L-9 requires describing biotic and abiotic features of specific Philippine ecosystems using labeled diagrams. There is no connection to living things, ecosystems, or labeled diagrams.

copy.en: Without air resistance, a golf ball and a cannonball with the same launch speed and angle would follow the same ideal parabolic path regardless of their mass.
copy.tl: Kung walang air resistance, ang golf ball at cannonball na may parehong launch speed at anggulo ay susunod sa parehong ideal parabolic path anuman ang kanilang mass.
copy.bis: Kung walay air resistance, ang golf ball ug cannonball nga adunay parehas nga launch speed ug anggulo mosunod sa parehas nga ideal parabolic path bisan unsa pa ang ilang mass.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The mass of a solution is simply the mass of the solute added to the mass of the solvent
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: research using secondary sources to identify how the properties of waves are described using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the mass of a solution (solute + solvent), a chemistry/matter concept. G6-F-6 is about describing wave properties (amplitude, frequency, wavelength, velocity) using secondary sources. There is no connection to waves or wave terminology.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The mass of a solution is simply the mass of the solute added to the mass of the solvent
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the relative wavelengths and frequencies of different types of electromagnetic waves, including radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultra-violet, x-rays, and gamma radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about solution mass, not electromagnetic waves. G9-F-11 requires comparing wavelengths and frequencies of different types of electromagnetic waves. The card provides no support for this competency.

copy.en: The mass of a solution is simply the mass of the solute added to the mass of the solvent, because both parts together make the whole.
copy.tl: Ang mass ng solution ay ang mass ng solute na idinagdag sa mass ng solvent, dahil ang dalawang bahagi na magkasama ang bumubuo sa kabuuan.
copy.bis: Ang mass sa solution mao ang mass sa solute nga gidugang sa mass sa solvent, tungod kay ang duha ka parte nga magkauban mao ang naghimo sa tibuok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A thermometer measures temperature, while a balance measures mass
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss the factors that limit the ecosystem's carrying capacity, such as adequate food, shelter, water, and mates
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about selecting appropriate measurement tools (thermometer vs balance). It has no content about ecosystem carrying capacity, limiting factors such as food, shelter, water, or mates.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A thermometer measures temperature, while a balance measures mass
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that the ecosystem's population growth slows down as it gets closer to the carrying capacity
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses measurement tools, not ecosystem population growth or carrying capacity. It provides no instructional support for this competency.

copy.en:
Why can't we use just one tool for every measurement?

Different samples need different tools. A thermometer measures temperature, while a balance measures mass, so you must choose the tool that matches what you are testing!
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi puwedeng isang tool lang ang gamitin sa lahat ng sukat?

Iba-ibang sample ang nangangailangan ng iba-ibang tool. Ang thermometer ay sumusukat ng temperature, habang ang balance ay sumusukat ng mass, kaya dapat piliin mo ang tool na tugma sa iyong sinusuri!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga dili man puwede nga usa ra ka tool ang gamiton sa tanang sukod?

Lain-laing sample ang nagkinahanglan ug lain-laing tool. Ang thermometer mosukod sa temperature, samtang ang balance mosukod sa mass, busa kinahanglan pilion nimo ang tool nga angay sa imong gisusi!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Paper, dried twigs, kerosene, cotton, paint thinner, alcohol, dried leaves, and tissue paper are highly flammable materials that catch fire easily.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that the arrangement of elements in the periodic table as 7 periods and 18 groups is based on their atomic structure and chemical properties, such as reactivity
assignedReviews.reason: The card lists common flammable materials; it does not address the periodic table's 7 periods and 18 groups, atomic structure, or chemical properties such as reactivity. The assigned competency is unrelated to the card's content.

copy.en: Paper, dried twigs, kerosene, cotton, paint thinner, alcohol, dried leaves, and tissue paper are highly flammable materials that catch fire easily.
copy.tl: Ang papel, tuyong sanga, kerosene, cotton, paint thinner, alcohol, tuyong dahon, at tissue paper ay mga highly flammable na materyales na madaling magliyab.
copy.bis: Ang papel, uga nga mga sanga, kerosene, cotton, paint thinner, alcohol, uga nga dahon, ug tissue paper mga highly flammable nga materyales nga dali ra nga modilaab.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the 100% leaf extract produced pigmentation on paper that was comparable to commercial ink
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a leaf extract (a liquid) used as ink and its pigmentation effect. G3-M-5 requires describing physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. The card provides no information about solid material properties and is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en:
Can a leaf extract really work like commercial ink?

In the mayana example, the 100% leaf extract produced pigmentation on paper that was comparable to commercial ink, making it a possible alternative source.
copy.tl:
Maaari bang gumana ang leaf extract tulad ng commercial ink?

Sa halimbawa ng mayana, ang 100% leaf extract ay nagdulot ng pigmentation sa papel na kasinghusay ng commercial ink, kaya maaari itong maging alternatibong pagkukunan.
copy.bis:
Mahimo ba nga ang leaf extract molihok sama sa commercial ink?

Sa pananglitan sa mayana, ang 100% leaf extract naghatag og pigmentation sa papel nga sama ka maayo sa commercial ink, busa mahimo kining alternatibong tinubdan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the rays hit the ground at a 90-degree angle
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the meaning of direct sunlight (rays at 90 degrees, concentrated energy). It has nothing to do with changes in temperature causing matter to change state (solid to liquid to gas). The topic is solar geometry, not matter state changes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the rays hit the ground at a 90-degree angle
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes direct rays of the Sun, not changes of state (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) using diagrams or flowcharts. No connection to matter state changes or the required representation.

copy.en:
What does it mean when the Sun's rays are 'direct'?

It means the rays hit the ground at a 90-degree angle, straight up and down, so the energy is concentrated on a small area.
copy.tl:
Ano ang ibig sabihin kapag 'direct' ang sinag ng araw?

Ibig sabihin, tumatama ang sinag sa lupa sa 90-degree angle, diretso pababa, kaya concentrated ang energy sa maliit na lugar.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pasabot kung 'direct' ang silaw sa adlaw?

Nagpasabot nga ang silaw moigo sa yuta sa 90-degree nga anggulo, tul-id paubos, busa ang energy nag-concentrate sa gamay nga lugar.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Electric charge is measured in coulombs, current in amperes, and power in watts.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: SI units for charge, current, and power are electricity, not plant reproduction.

copy.en: Electric charge is measured in coulombs, current in amperes, and power in watts.
copy.tl: Ang electric charge ay sinusukat sa coulombs, ang current sa amperes, at ang power sa watts.
copy.bis: Ang electric charge gisukod sa coulombs, ang current sa amperes, ug ang power sa watts.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Leaves have both length and width that can be measured with tools, and width is measured across the widest part of the leaf blade
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: Measuring leaf width is unrelated to how living things depend on one another to meet their basic needs.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Leaves have both length and width that can be measured with tools, and width is measured across the widest part of the leaf blade
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web
assignedReviews.reason: Measuring leaf width is unrelated to producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web.

copy.en:
How do I measure the width of a leaf?

Measure across the widest part, from one edge to the other, using a ruler.
copy.tl:
Paano ko sinusukat ang lapad ng dahon?

Sukatin mo ito sa pinakamalawak na bahagi, mula sa isang gilid hanggang sa kabilang gilid, gamit ang ruler.
copy.bis:
Unsaon nako pagsukod sa gilapdon sa dahon?

Sukda kini sa pinakalapad nga parte, sugod sa usa ka kilid paingon sa pikas kilid, gamit ang ruler.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A balance measures mass, the amount of matter in an object
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches how a balance measures mass, which is a measurement/physics concept. It does not address the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter) at all.

copy.en:
How do you find the mass of a small rock?

Use an electronic balance or a triple beam balance, and the answer will be in kilograms or grams.
copy.tl:
Paano mo malalaman ang mass ng maliit na bato?

Gumamit ng electronic balance o triple beam balance, at ang sagot ay nasa kilograms o grams.
copy.bis:
Giunsa nimo pagkahibalo ang mass sa gamay nga bato?

Gamita ang electronic balance o triple beam balance, ug ang tubag kay naa sa kilograms o grams.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Media literacy skills
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in solid materials make them useful, such as when they are shaped, pressed, hammered, joined, or cut
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses media literacy and evaluating typhoon advisories, which has no relation to describing how changes in solid materials make them useful (shaped, pressed, hammered, joined, cut).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Media literacy skills
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: determine how forces can change the shape of objects such as when they are pushed, pulled, stretched, bent, twisted, or squeezed
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about checking information sources and rumor verification, not about forces changing the shape of objects. No instructional support for this competency.

copy.en: Media literacy skills help you check who posted the information, compare it with official sources, and decide whether a typhoon advisory is reliable or just a rumor.
copy.tl: Ang media literacy skills ay tumutulong sa iyo na tingnan kung sino ang nag-post ng impormasyon, ikumpara ito sa opisyal na source, at magpasya kung maaasahan ang isang typhoon advisory o tsismis lang.
copy.bis: Ang media literacy skills makatabang nimo nga tan-awon kinsa ang nag-post sa impormasyon, ikumpara kini sa opisyal nga source, ug magdesisyon kon kasaligan ba ang usa ka typhoon advisory o hungihong lang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: By classifying organisms, scientists can discover new pharmaceutical compounds from natural sources like plants, fungi, and marine animals.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses taxonomy and pharmaceutical discovery from natural sources, which has no instructional support for describing how the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems work. The assigned competency is about human body systems, and the card does not mention any body system.

copy.en: By classifying organisms, scientists can discover new pharmaceutical compounds from natural sources like plants, fungi, and marine animals.
copy.tl: Sa pamamagitan ng pag-uuri ng mga organismo, ang mga scientist ay makakatuklas ng mga bagong pharmaceutical compound mula sa kalikasan tulad ng mga halaman, fungi, at mga hayop sa dagat.
copy.bis: Pinaagi sa pagklasipika sa mga organismo, ang mga scientist makadiskobre ug bag-ong pharmaceutical compounds gikan sa kinaiyahan sama sa mga tanom, fungi, ug mga mananap sa dagat.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Meerkats make their home in the hot, dry deserts of southern Africa, like the Kalahari.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires a drawing or diagram classifying Philippine animals/plants by habitat (terrestrial, aquatic, aerial). The card is a single factual statement about meerkats in African deserts, with no drawing/diagram and no Philippine species, so it does not support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Meerkats make their home in the hot, dry deserts of southern Africa, like the Kalahari.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a list or draw up a table with examples of animals and plants in a particular habitat, such as a garden, rice field, seashore, and mangrove swamp
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires making a list or table of animals and plants in a particular habitat (e.g., garden, rice field, seashore, mangrove swamp). The card provides no list/table and names only one animal in a non-Philippine habitat, so it does not support the competency.

copy.en: Meerkats make their home in the hot, dry deserts of southern Africa, like the Kalahari.
copy.tl: Naninirahan ang mga meerkat sa mainit at tuyong disyerto ng timog Africa, tulad ng Kalahari.
